newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SKI FLYING-OKABE SWOOPS TO GOLD, SMASHES RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SKI FLYING-OKABE SWOOPS TO GOLD, SMASHES RECORD.

text.p: Japan's Takanobu Okabe wrapped up a day of firsts on Saturday when he took gold at the World Cup ski-flying competition and flew a record distance on the world's largest natural ski jump.
Okabe, who smashed the famous Kulm's record of 201 metres with a leap of 205 in training, beat local hero Andreas Goldberger with jumps of 198.5 and 196 to total 379.9 points.

But Slovenia's 17-year-old Primoz Peterka was also celebrating after a spectacular second jump of 195.5 metres lifted him into the bronze position from fifth, putting him top of the World Cup standings with 997 points.
Germany's Dieter Thoma, who decided against competing in order to prepare for Trondheim, is second just 13 points behind, followed by Okabe with 740.
Peterka and his rivals will get another chance to boost their world ranking in Thoma's absence when the competition continues on Sunday.
